messages:
Alex R.: heads-up — LogStream just posted an advisory: potential exposure of API ingestion keys for a subset of customers. link: https://status.logstream.example/incidents/2024-03-05 :warning:
Maria S.: @channel do we have any keys that were sent to LogStream (service account / ingestion credentials)?
Derek T.: short answer: yes — we use a LogStream forwarder for app logs in staging and one ingest key in prod for metrics. I'll pull inventory now.
Sophia L.: tagging eng-security — we need an initial exposure assessment. prioritize KMS-wrapped keys and any plaintext cred artifacts in S3.
ops-bot: Incident alert created: VS-2024-03-05-001 (vendor-logstream). Assigned: Derek T., Severity: P2.
Alex R.: Derek — do we have the key IDs? which KMS customer key was used for wrapping?
Derek T.: found entry in config repo: LOGSTREAM_KEY_ID = projects/redwood/kms/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/logstream-prod-1
Maria S.: can you run a quick check for any recent decrypts/usage? pull Cloud KMS audit log for that key.
Derek T.: running. snippet of CloudAudit logs I see: ```protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" resourceName="projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/logstream-prod-1/cryptoKeyVersions/1"```
Alex R.: timeline please — any decrypts from unfamiliar IPs or service accounts?
Derek T.: decrypts from our forwarder service account logstream-ingest@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com between 2024-03-04T22:10Z and 2024-03-04T22:45Z. No obvious unknown IPs yet but one decrypt looks from an ephemeral IP that isn't in our allowed egress list.
Sophia L.: containment: rotate the ingest key, revoke forwarder service account tokens, revoke any associated API tokens with LogStream, and put the forwarder on hold. Maria — can you draft comms to compliance?
Maria S.: on it. Also we'll need to rotate any downstream client keys and rotate KMS ciphertexts that were shared with LogStream. I'll start an emergency RFC to rotate: kms/rotate-logstream-20240305.
Alex R.: Derek — can you disable the LogStream integration in prod for the next 2 hours and switch logs to local buffering? add a canary to watch SLOs.
Derek T.: done — feature flag toggled: LOGSTREAM_INGEST_ENABLED=false. Local buffering enabled. Monitoring: created alert for log backlog > 5m.
ops-bot: Deployment event: feature-flag update pushed to prod by Derek T. (id: deploy-8843)
Maria S.: legal/compliance question: do we need to notify customers? depends on LogStream's root cause and whether customer data was included. I'm drafting notification criteria now.
Sophia L.: ask LogStream for:
- full forensic timeline
- list of exposed keys/IDs
- IOCs and IPs
- whether any KMS ciphertexts were exfiltrated
- exact scope of customer IDs
Also request that they rotate ingestion keys on their side and confirm.
Alex R.: also ask vendor to provide signed attestation and their mitigation steps and a timeline for root cause fix. We should get an SLA for forensic deliverables.
Derek T.: quick vuln triage notes: our forwarder stores only the encrypted key (ciphertext) and the service account token. If LogStream got plaintext API keys by their ingestion pipeline, worst case is API token compromise. We must assume keys leaked until proven otherwise.
Maria S.: action item list added to incident doc VS-2024-03-05-001:
- Rotate KMS key logstream-prod-1 and re-encrypt any ciphertexts (Derek)
- Revoke forwarder SA keys and issue new SA with minimal RBAC (Alex)
- Rotate any API tokens sent to LogStream (Product/SRE)
- Collect KMS audit logs + LogStream's IOCs (Sophia)
- Customer notification draft (Maria)
- Postmortem owner assigned (Sophia)
Alex R.: RBAC follow-up: after rotation create a scoped service account with only decrypt on that specific key and ensure key access is audited and requires 2-person approval for production changes.
Sophia L.: long term: add inline validation to prevent plaintext ingestion keys from being sent to third parties and enforce encryption-at-rest on any log shipping. Also add a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rule to block patterns that look like API keys.
Maria S.: update — LogStream replied: they reported internal log exposure from a misconfigured retention job; they claim only rotated ingestion tokens were present. they've provided an initial timeline and list of 4 IPs. Attaching their PDF in the incident doc.
Derek T.: matched two IPs to known LogStream worker ranges. one IP remains unknown — blocked at perimeter and added to blacklist.
Alex R.: next steps before we close:
1) Confirm no plaintext keys in our S3 logs and rotate any tokens that could be impacted.
2) Formal vendor attestation + signed timeline.
3) Postmortem with corrective actions (RBAC changes, KMS policies, DLP, audit retention increase).
Maria S.: I'll sync with support and product for customer comms. Draft will be ready in 90 minutes.
Sophia L.: assigning postmortem to me. I'll schedule a 1-hr blameless review tomorrow and include vendor findings.
Alex R.: thanks team. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
